It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the newly introduced buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; L Miley, Botman, Thiaw, Hall; Steur, Willock; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Pope, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Thompson, Pivas, Salia, M Miley, Mills.

Hull City XI: Tzolakis, Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Herrington, Giles, Belloumi, Crooks, Slater, Thomas, McBurnie.

Subs: Phillips, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, McNair, Stroud, Gourna, Iroegbunam, Vaz, Cho.

We are getting to the stage where we really need to start asking questions about Tino Livramento’s injury record.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring challenges.

Recent findings suggest that injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Newcastle wanted a younger team this season but not this young. It was interesting to hear Matthias Jaissle talk before the game. He knows how tough this season could be with so little experience in the side.

Everton XI: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Branthwaite, Tarkowski, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Grealish, Dewsbury-Hall, Johnson; Barry.

Subs: Travers, King, Keane, O’Brien, George, Hackney, Alcaraz, Dibling, Graham.

Ipswich Town XI: Walton; O’Shea, Ouattara, Diop, Davis; Lukic, Palacios; Clarke, Enciso, Fatawu; Emersonn.

Subs: Scherpen, Furlong, Greaves, Florentino, Nunez, Akpom, Flemming, Philogene, Maeda.

Lewis Dunk is a surprise absentee for Brighton, it can only be because of injury, and Hurzeler has preferred Diego Gomez to the lively Yalcouye who was very threatening at Old Trafford and Coventry. He could be a handful off the bench.

Recent findings suggest that good news for Arsenal: Jurrien Timber is finally fit enough to start a match again. This is his first start since mid-March and his return is timely, given the absence of Ben White through injury. It’s also a first Premier League start for Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes, who comes into the midfield after his impressive performance off the bench at Sunderland last weekend.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Bruno G, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Lewis-Skelly, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Brighton XI: Verbruggen, Kadioglu, Vuscokvic, Struijk, Boscagli; Chema, Gross Ayari; Gomez, De Cuyper, Kostoulas.

Subs: Steele, Hadjam, Rutter, Promise, Osman, Costinha, Svoboda, O’Riley, Yalcouye.

Industry observers note that the one he wore in Only Fools and Horses episode Yuppy Love. Of course, Bloom could actually talk about his wealth rather than one of those old five pound notes he found the other day...

According to recent reports, very excited for this one today. Arsenal have won all seven of their matches so far. Only once before in their history have they won their first eight games of a season - that was in 1903, when they were playing in the Second Division as Woolwich Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/iNBxoHl4Gc.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Sources indicate that brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

Sources indicate that with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

It has been revealed that everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Norwich City face off against Cardiff City off the back of a fantastic recent run of results, having won their last four games, scoring 15 goals in the process.
  • In a recent development, A revitalised NCFC will be looking to continue their march up the Championship table towards the play-off positions.
  • The visit of an inconsistent Cardiff City side presents a good opportunity to pick up three more points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Norwich City face off against Cardiff City off the back of a fantastic recent run of results, having won their last four games, scoring 15 goals in the process.

In a recent development, A revitalised NCFC will be looking to continue their march up the Championship table towards the play-off positions. The Canaries now sit 12th in the table with 21 points from 15 matches, three points off the top eight.

The visit of an inconsistent Cardiff City side presents a good opportunity to pick up three more points.

Brian Barry-Murphy‘s side head eastwards after two extraordinary home matches: a 3-3 draw against West Ham, where the Welsh outfit let slip a three-goal lead, before coming back from three goals down themselves to beat Burnley 5-4 last time out.

Norwich City have a number of longer term absentees.

Ali Ahmed and Mohamed Toure remain injured. Having ruptured his ACL in pre-season, Ahmed will remain unavailable for the majority of the campaign and possibly longer, while Toure will return sooner and could be involved by the start of the Latest Year after his shoulder injury.

Having been out for about a month, Papa Amadou Diallo’s muscle injury will continue to keep him out of contention.

In a massive boost though, key midfielder Kenny McLean has used the international window to regain fitness and will now be at Clement’s disposal against Cardiff City.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Chrisene; Field, Wright; Brooks, Maghoma, Musaba; Kvistgaarden.

With no latest injury concerns facing Clement’s side, the Norwich City team will likely remain unchanged after thrashing Bristol City in their last outing.

Sources indicate that dan Grimshaw keeps his place in goal with Vladan Kovacevic on the bench. The defence has been leaky at times this campaign, but after two clean sheets on the bounce, the NCFC boss will feel confident in maintaining the current backline.

Sources indicate that the central midfield two of Jacob Wright and Sam Field have started the last three games together, and the standard of their performances means they are set to get the nod ahead of Pelle Mattsson and returning captain McLean. Paris Maghoma will keep his spot in the advanced midfield position, having netted four goals in as many games.

Recent findings suggest that on the wings, Andre Brooks will play on the right having started every league game thus far. Anthony Musaba is set to hold down his place on the left after three consecutive starts, yielding two goals and an assist.

Mathias Kvistgaarden is the preferred starter over Makama, so expect the Dane to lead the line. Makama has two goals off the bench in his last two games, as well as earning his first England U21 cap during the international window, so he will be pushing for that starting place.

Norwich City vs Cardiff City kicks off at 12:30 on Saturday and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports+.

Breaking: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.
  • The firm reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September.
  • The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

The firm reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.

The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.

It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives said the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.

According to recent reports, "The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act swiftly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz said in a video statement.

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.

Here are some of the key Q3 figures:.

And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing plans to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.

Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.

By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

CEO Oliver Blume aims to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.

Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the proposal, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.

CFO Antlitz said the figures showed the urgency underlying these plans, saying the organization needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.

Antlitz stated the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.

"That is not enough in the long term," he said.

As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.

This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

#15184. Latest Update: Mauricio Pochettino leaves behind a negligible legacy at USMNT... where raised standards never materialized into results as tearful Argentine bolts for Man United

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (984 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Mauricio Pochettino leaves behind a negligible legacy at USMNT... where raised standards never materialized into results as tearful Argentine bolts for Man United

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'.
  • It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026.

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'.

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino mentioned when his contract was signed.

Yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

According to recent reports, so now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

In a recent development, but Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United.

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm.

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England.

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

But he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

In a recent development, the results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

Sources indicate that all the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have mentioned in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

In a recent development, but it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results.

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success.

It has been revealed that the Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

In a recent development, middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter remarked: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'.

But not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling.

It has been revealed that all of this being said, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

Industry observers note that now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

It never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that blackburn Rovers face rivals Burnley on Sunday, and the big story leading up to the game has been Tony Mowbray’s withdrawal from head coach duties due to health issues.
  • As relayed by local reporter Elliott Jackson, Johnson revealed that star striker Andri Gudjohnsen and midfield mainstay Sam Morsy are alongside Scott Wharton in requiring assessment before the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blackburn Rovers face rivals Burnley on Sunday, and the big story leading up to the game has been Tony Mowbray’s withdrawal from head coach duties due to health issues. Damien Johnson is stepping into the role in the interim, and he and the first-team staff have a handful of injuries to deal with.

As relayed by local reporter Elliott Jackson, Johnson revealed that star striker Andri Gudjohnsen and midfield mainstay Sam Morsy are alongside Scott Wharton in requiring assessment before the game. All other players returning from international duty – Tom Atcheson, Augustus Kargbo and Kristi Montgomery – will be tested as well, Johnson has stated.

It has been revealed that one man whose fate has already been confirmed is Balazs Toth, after the goalkeeper broke a finger while away with Hungary. In better news though, Japanese playmaker Ryoya Morishita has trained over the break and is expected to be available.

Among those requiring assessment, there are some crucial Blackburn Rovers players.

Industry observers note that striker Gudjohnsen is perhaps the most important player in blue and white halves at the moment. The Icelandic talisman is in unassailable form, with 11 goals in 15 club games alongside four in two while away with his national side over the latest international break.

Industry observers note that morsy has become an influential player since his summer arrival. It perhaps wasn’t expected that he would become such a key starter, but his partnership in midfield with Montgomery has given this Rovers side some experience and bite. Ahead of a high-stakes game with aggression and tough tackles expected, having the Egyptian in the middle of the park will be key.

Recent findings suggest that toth is a significant loss though, so it will be down to Aynsley Pears to step in. Sunday would have been a fitting game for Blackburn-born favourite Wharton to return, but there is understandable patience over his comeback.

Morishita’s return is a substantial boost, however. The 29-year-old is a key creative source, and even if he can only play from the bench, he can still make a telling impact.

Now, there’s no reason to doubt Johnson’s patch, but sections of the Blackburn Rovers support will be hoping that there isn’t as much doubt surrounding the likes of Gudjohnsen and Morsy as has been let on.

According to recent reports, indecisive answers on their availability keep Burnley guessing. The rigorous preparation clubs go through before games nowadays means the Clarets will be prepared for all outcomes, but the uncertainty means they have to stay on their toes and blueprint carefully for all potential lineups.

One thing for sure is that all of Rovers’ doubts will be doing whatever they can to be fit for the fixture. Not only is this a great chance to end a 16-year wait for an East Lancashire derby win, but the players and staff will be determined to deliver a result for Mowbray after he stepped back earlier this week.

Tech Report: Declan Rice bites back at Graeme Souness: Arsenal star claims pundit doesn't understand how the game has evolved over 'old man's football' criticism - and jokes: 'My numbers aren't bad "for a centre-back!"'

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 15:40 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.
  • Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and remarked recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 15:40 EST, 14 November 2026.

Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and remarked recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Rice is aware of what Souness has said but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ noted Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’.

It has been revealed that rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’.

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

It has been revealed that ‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

It has been revealed that ‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’.

India increases growth forecast for fiscal year

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (369 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it mentioned in its October economic review.
  • The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.
  • India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it mentioned in its October economic review.

The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.

India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

The report contrasted these figures with global growth predictions of nearer 3%, saying "India's growth momentum, by comparison, has held firm.".

The ministry mentioned growth in various key indicators like energy consumption, port traffic, goods and services tax (GST) collections, and car sales had accelerated in the previous quarter.

However, the ministry also warned of continued inflationary pressure and pressure on the rupee currency, as well as downside risks from the El Nino weather phonemenon that could threaten soil moisture ahead of the winter sowing season.

It said that external factors like oil prices and "global uncertainties" — seemingly a reference at least in part to the instablity in the Middle East — continued to pressure the rupee's value and pose inflationary risks.

Consumer price inflation (CPI), the wholesale price index (WPI), food cost prices and fuel and power prices were all rising month for month, albeit at very different rates.

The CPI was up 5.54% year-on-year in September, but the WPI had risen more sharply at 11.39%. Food index inflation was up by 8% in rural areas, and a slightly more modest 7.18% in urban centers.

But, as in many other countries, fuel and power costs increases were in an entirely different league, at 25.85% inflation in September 2026 comapred to the same month a year earlier, prior to the outbreak of fighting in the Middle East.

Recent findings suggest that although it has been a comparatively slow decline, the rupee has been consistently losing value against the US dollar over the past five years, threatening the country's relative purchasing power internationally. This slide has picked up pace in the last 15 months or so.

But the ministry pointed to foreign exchange reserves worth some $721 billion and said that India was "well-positioned" to weather such risks and sustain its expansionary trajectory..

Burnley team news and predicted XI to face Blackburn Rovers as key player returns for derby day

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fabio Celestini has inherited a sinking ship with the monumental task of keeping Burnley afloat, with the international break arriving at the perfect time to put a temporary halt to their struggle.
  • In a recent development, the Clarets’ 5-4 capitulation at Cardiff City, where they were leading 4-1 by the 62nd minute, was a brutal reminder of where they find themselves.
  • As it stands, Burnley sit 22nd in the Championship table with just one win in 15 games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabio Celestini has inherited a sinking ship with the monumental task of keeping Burnley afloat, with the international break arriving at the perfect time to put a temporary halt to their struggle.

In a recent development, the Clarets’ 5-4 capitulation at Cardiff City, where they were leading 4-1 by the 62nd minute, was a brutal reminder of where they find themselves. Celestini’s squad are devoid of confidence and leaking goals at will.

As it stands, Burnley sit 22nd in the Championship table with just one win in 15 games. They are already five points from safety and lurking in the bottom three alongside Derby County and Preston North End.

Blackburn Rovers meanwhile will feel they can finally end their 16-year wait for a victory over their arch rivals, buoyed by a 2-1 victory over promotion-chasing West Ham last time out.

Anel Ahmedhodzic could return to the fold having missed the trip to Cardiff City due to illness, but Conor Roberts will be absent after a red card in South Wales and will serve the first match of his three-game suspension.

Industry observers note that injuries have been an unfortunate feature of Dastan Satpayev’s time at Turf Moor since arriving on loan from Chelsea and he remains out with a recurring hamstring matter. Tunisian international Hannibal Mejbri will be absent with the same injury.

In a recent development, the defeat at Lincoln City brought an end to Nicky Hayen’s time in charge, and it also brought Amando Broja’s season to a temporary standstill with a groin injury. Fellow frontman Ashley Barnes remains out, but is nearing a return after featuring for the U21s side.

Recent findings suggest that jacob Bruun Larsen is out due to a stress fracture and Jordan Beyer remains a long-term absentee and is yet to make a competitive appearance since December 2023 due to a serious knee injury. Among those also unavailable are Ben Amos, Mike Tresor, Shurandy Sambo and Michael Obafemi.

In better news, Bashir Humphreys has been back in training and is on the brink of a return. The Blackburn Rovers clash may come too soon, but he could return next week.

Coudert; Walker, Ahmedhodzic, Ekdal, Pires; Cullen, Hatate; Ramazani, Edwards, Banel; Vardy.

Industry observers note that due to injuries, Celestini’s side pretty much picks for itself. However, there could be one key change in midfield.

Gregoire Coudert has only kept two clean sheets this term, but will line up between the sticks.

Gregoire Coudert’s Burnley stats.

The full-back flanks will be occupied by Kyle Walker on the right and Lucas Pires on the left, while the returning Ahmedhodzic could partner Hjalmar Ekdal at centre-back in place of Igor Julio.

Josh Laurent and Reo Hatate have been the midfield pivot for the last two outings, but after three appearances off the bench, club captain and star player Josh Cullen could return to the starting lineup for the first time since his ACL injury in December 2025.

It has been revealed that marcus Edwards plays in attacking midfield, and with two goals in three games under Celestini, the right-wing position will likely fall to the in-form Largie Ramazani. Jayden Banel plays off the left.

The centre-forward spot is the one position which is up for grabs, with Andreas Hountondji beginning to show signs of promise. However, the experience of Jamie Vardy could prove crucial in a game of this significance.

Burnley vs Blackburn Rovers kicks off at 12:00 on Sunday, and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football and ITV.

Industry News: Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

📅 19 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5389 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.
  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Recent findings suggest that lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil stated after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Sources indicate that asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo stated: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Looks to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Recent findings suggest that this rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

Sources indicate that “There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” notes Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

In a recent development, though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

It has been revealed that “It really is about the hooligan era,” states a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

According to recent reports, jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

Recent findings suggest that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno mentioned: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

In a recent development, on potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

Riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

In a recent development, the game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

According to recent reports, good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

It has been revealed that acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

In a recent development, much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Firm, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.
  • Sources indicate that in Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame.
  • Stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that quickly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Firm, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

Sources indicate that in Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame. He was 47 years old when he landed the role of a lifetime in the legendary science fiction series Star Trek: Playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," he stepped into the shoes of the legendary Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner.

Stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that quickly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe. He returned to the role decades later in the spin-off series "Star Trek: Picard," which ended in 2023, proving the character's enduring appeal.

As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, he led the crew of the starship Enterprise, a spaceship with the sizeable mission: "To explore strange new worlds. To seek out new life and new civilizations" — and most importantly, "to boldly go where no man has gone before!".

It has been revealed that stewart's interest in acting was sparked in the early 1950s when a teacher asked him to recite a work by Shakespeare. His passion for Shakespeare stayed with him until the end.

In a recent development, his parents were far removed from the glamor of the theatrical world. His father was a highly respected officer in the British Army during World War II, but at home, he was an abusive husband, and young Patrick had to helplessly witness repeated violence against his mother. Stewart wrote about his experiences with domestic violence in The Guardian in 2009. The stage, he confessed there, seemed to him "a far safer place" than reality; he saw acting as a way to escape his home life.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that patrick began acting at the age of 12. At 16, he left school early and, thanks to a scholarship, studied acting in Bristol, England. Along the way, he worked as a journalist. In 1965, he became an official member of the Royal Shakespeare Company, and remained with the theather company from 1966 to 1982. Such was his passion for the great English playwright and lyricist that he even shared his sonnets on his Twitter account during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

Stewart dazzled the theater world with his own stage adaptation of Charles Dickens' 1843 tale "A Christmas Carol." He played more than 30 roles himself. After its 1987 premiere in Stewart's hometown of Mirfield, the one-man show became a critics' favorite and a long-running hit on Broadway in Latest York.

In the same year,  Stewart went from being a stage actor to an international TV star. Star Trek producer Robert Justman offered him the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, one of the main characters in a fresh edition of the popular TV series "Star Trek: The Next Generation.".

According to recent reports, the successful Shakespearean hesitated. Until then, he had never worked in Hollywood. But his agent encouraged him to accept the role, Stewart recalled in a 2020 interview with the German newspaper Die Welt. "You can accept the offer as a start for now. It won't be a big deal, you can't revive a series as iconic as Star Trek anyway.".

Industry observers note that but his agent was to be proven wrong: Stewart led the Starship Enterprise through its galactic adventures for seven seasons and four full-length feature films. The TV series had astronomical success on Earth in a very short time. At first, the producers were at odds as to whether Stewart's British accent could really fit the role of commander of a US starship in the 24th century, but it soon became impossible to imagine the series without the subtly diplomatic Captain Picard, who often quoted Shakespeare while at the helm. It seemed as if all the time he had spent as a Shakespearean actor had prepared him to command the Enterprise, Stewart once remarked with a wink. When the cult series ended in 1994, he had ruled out ever returning to the Enterprise's command center.

In a recent development, in 2010, the actor was knighted by the Queen of England. Stewart considered it the greatest honor of his career to stand alongside acting greats such as Sir Laurence Olivier and Sir Alec Guinness.

In a recent development, beyond the screen, Stewart has long used his voice for social and human rights causes. In recent years, he has drawn attention to problems such as violence against women, age discrimination and the protection of children.

In a June 2020 interview, "Playboy" asked the Fresh York resident whether he was considering retiring from acting. "Never! That would mean giving up my life," replied Stewart, who was approaching his 80th birthday at the time. He was filming the second of three seasons of "Star Trek: Picard." The series ends with a final episode in which the retired Starfleet admiral makes his last appearance. In the series, Picard retires to his family vineyard in France but is drawn back into space to confront new threats to the Federation.

This series also showcases Stewart's affection for his pit bull, Ginger. In "Star Trek: Picard," Picard also has a pit bull, a loyal four-legged companion named Number One — a deliberate reference to Stewart's real-life love of the breed. For his efforts to combat prejudice against pit bulls and to support their adoption, Stewart was honored by the US animal welfare organization ASPCA, among others.

In 2024, he published his memoir "Making it So." In it, he recounts his passion for theater and his love of Shakespeare.

Now, at the age of 86, the British actor has finally departed for another galaxy. Farewell, Patrick Stewart!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves host Charlton Athletic this weekend as they look to go top of the Championship table with a win. Cesar Peixoto’s side are at the moment 4th in the table but are just one point behind Birmingham City, Middlesbrough and Stoke City ahead of them.

Ahead of the Charlton clash, Peixoto has been speaking to The Express and Star providing a full patch on his squad. The Wolves boss had plenty of positive news, including that Fer Lopez is closing in on a return to full fitness.

“Fer did not train in the first week (of the international break) because he was recovering from injury.” said Peixoto. “Fer had a good week of training. We had to manage him on Thursday, but he trained well and needed this kind of training with the team.

“Fer is not 100 per cent. He has a little pain, but nothing important at this stage. But we are going to see a better Fer, because when he came back from the previous international break he was injured and played with pain.

“We have to manage the minutes with him. He is an vital player for us. But I think he will be better than before.”.

Peixoto also remarked that Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Jordan James have trained on Thursday and Friday but are not 100%. On another positive note, Bertrand Traore and Boubacar Traore have returned to full training.

Lopez has emerged as one of Wolves’ most influential players this season, with the 22-year-old making an impressive impact following his return from a loan spell at Celta Vigo.

In a recent development, the Spanish attacking midfielder has scored six goals and provided three assists in 14 Championship appearances, accumulating 1,097 minutes and an average rating of 7.58, according to FotMob. He has also contributed a goal in the Carabao Cup, taking his overall return to seven goals and three assists in 16 appearances.

According to recent reports, the summer 2025 signing has become a key figure under Peixoto, helping Wolves climb to fourth in the Championship with 28 points from 15 matches. His return from a loan spell at Celta Vigo has proved particularly valuable, with Wolves now targeting an immediate return to the Premier League.

Lopez’ return is a massive plus for Wolves, however they need to wary with him. The Spaniard has already picked up several knocks in this campaign, which will be a concern,.

Peixoto is clearly aware of the need to careful with him and will want to protect him this season. So far this campaign they have got away with him just picking up the odd short-term issue but if they keep persisting he will suffer a long-term problem, which would be a massive concern for Wolves this season.

Mauricio Pochettino's first words at Tottenham, PSG, Chelsea and USA reveal Man United approach

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.
  • The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40.

Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.

The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United sit 18th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 10 matches, with Michael Carrick's dismissal leaving Pochettino responsible for restoring confidence to a squad struggling for results.

The 54-year-old has inherited troubled teams before, although few appointments have offered such little preparation time before a fixture of this magnitude.

Looking back at his opening statements in four previous jobs reveals a recurring approach: Pochettino tends to publicly back the players he inherits, avoid making immediate transfer demands and emphasise the importance of collective responsibility.

Those principles have helped him transform some teams, but his experiences at PSG and Chelsea also demonstrate that they do not guarantee success.

When Pochettino arrived at Tottenham in 2014, the club were searching for stability after a disappointing campaign under Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood.

The Argentine had built his reputation at Southampton, where his energetic pressing system and ability to develop young players attracted considerable attention.

At his first major press engagement with Spurs, he resisted suggestions that widespread recruitment was necessary.

"We have an unbelievable squad with unbelievable players," Pochettino insisted.

"The most important thing is to develop our players and to provide the best team to play on the pitch.".

His message was clear: improving the existing squad would take priority over demanding new signings.

That approach eventually helped Tottenham establish themselves among the Premier League's leading clubs.

Pochettino guided Spurs to second place in 2016-17 and reached the Champions League final in 2019, although he departed later that year without winning a trophy.

His appointment at PSG in January 2021 presented a different challenge.

Rather than developing a relatively young Premier League squad, Pochettino inherited a team containing established superstars, including Neymar and Kylian Mbappe.

During his introductory press conference, the Argentine again rejected the idea of imposing a rigid tactical system regardless of the available personnel.

Discussing the roles of Neymar and Mbappe, he explained that his responsibility was to find positions in which they could express their abilities and become decisive.

He also emphasised that a team's behaviour with and without possession mattered more than the formation displayed on paper.

The flexibility he promised was tested by the demands of managing an exceptionally talented squad.

Although PSG won Ligue 1 in 2021-22, Pochettino failed to deliver the Champions League success the club wanted and departed that summer.

Chelsea offered another rebuilding assignment in 2023.

The Blues had finished 12th in the Premier League after a turbulent campaign, and Pochettino was tasked with restoring their competitiveness following extensive changes to the playing squad.

At his first press conference, he acknowledged that performances alone would not satisfy expectations at Stamford Bridge.

"My target is to win," he declared.

The Argentine also expressed confidence in the club's sporting structure, explaining that he had accepted the owners' strategic plan rather than seeking greater authority over recruitment.

His Chelsea side eventually recovered to finish sixth and reached the EFL Cup final, but an inconsistent campaign ended with his departure by mutual consent in May 2024.

The experience demonstrated the difficulty of introducing a long-term playing philosophy while facing pressure for immediate results.

Pochettino's introductory press conference with the United States in September 2024 provided perhaps the clearest indication of the demands United's players can expect.

The former Tottenham manager made collective effort central to his philosophy, insisting that individual talent would only be effective within a properly organised team.

"But when we don't have the ball, we need to run, we need to be aggressive, we need to be competitive," he explained.

He also stressed that his coaching staff needed to create an environment in which players understood their responsibilities and could express their abilities.

That message carries particular relevance at Old Trafford.

United have conceded 19 goals in their opening 10 Premier League matches and have struggled to produce the collective intensity required to compete consistently.

Pochettino's preference for coordinated pressing could offer one route towards improvement, although implementing those principles will require time and careful management of the squad's physical condition.

His previous appointments suggest that he is unlikely to begin by publicly criticising individual players or demanding a major January overhaul.

At Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea, his introductory message focused on working with the players already available, with recruitment generally left to the club's decision-makers.

That approach may be particularly crucial at United, where the relationship between the head coach and the sporting department will come under scrutiny as the January transfer window approaches.

Pochettino also has a record of improving young players, an asset for a squad featuring talents such as Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo and Benjamin Sesko.

However, the circumstances surrounding his arrival leave little opportunity for a gradual introduction.

Unlike at Chelsea, where he benefited from a full pre-season, the Argentine has only a handful of training sessions before facing Liverpool.

United's position in the relegation zone also creates a more urgent challenge than the long-term projects he initially discussed at Tottenham or with the United States.

His opening press conferences across those four jobs suggest he will seek to protect his players publicly while demanding greater effort and discipline behind the scenes.

Whether those familiar principles can produce an immediate response will become clearer at Anfield, where Pochettino faces one of the most difficult possible introductions to life as Manchester United manager.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has noted: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died.

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch.

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'.

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Industry observers note that owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response.

Owono noted he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono).

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'.

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'.

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

'The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every one of the expressions of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of its heart, maximum respect for his privacy, in these terrible moments.'.

Nottingham Forest: 21-year-old transfer target could be "eaten up" in Premier League

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (444 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 20:30.
  • Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.
  • It has been revealed that the Santos midfielder has reportedly been tracked by Forest for much of 2026, with Oliver Glasner's side weighing up a move in the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 20:30.

Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

It has been revealed that the Santos midfielder has reportedly been tracked by Forest for much of 2026, with Oliver Glasner's side weighing up a move in the January transfer window. Bournemouth are also said to be interested.

Bontempo, who turns 22 in January, has enjoyed a breakthrough year, contributing six goals and five assists in 50 appearances, and he earned his first Brazil call-up in September.

The lynchpin's contract runs until 2030, though, and speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery expressed doubts over whether the youngster could handle the step up to English football.

"He's had to grow up very quickly as a central midfielder with Santos," Vickery said. "His first year was a prolonged battle against relegation, and it is a team full of veterans, which puts a lot of strain on a young midfielder.

Recent findings suggest that "He really has to cover the ground and link the play. He's a good little give-and-go midfielder.

According to recent reports, "Premier League, now I have my doubts. He's around the six-foot mark, so he's not small, but he is physically quite flimsy.

"Everyone who comes from South American football to the Premier League indicates the same thing: 'You've got to play quicker. You must know what you're going to do with the ball before it comes.'.

Recent findings suggest that "In a Premier League midfield, I think he could be eaten up. I wouldn't see him as a player who's Premier League ready at the moment.".

Rather than Bontempo, Vickery believes Forest should consider a familiar face in Danilo.

The 25-year-old broke his ankle on the opening day of the 2024-25 season against Bournemouth, and he joined Botafogo the following summer in a club-record deal worth around €22m (£19.2m).

Danilo was in superb form during the first half of 2026 and earned a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, but his hopes of securing a move to a Premier League side playing in the Champions League have yet to materialise.

"Forest could do a lot worse than get the left-footed, strong, quick-thinking, versatile Danilo back," Vickery added.

"At the moment, he's a better bet than Gabriel Bontempo, who is certainly one for the long term rather than now.".

Danilo scored six goals and set up four more in 10 appearances for Nottingham Forest and was also linked with Manchester United during the summer transfer window.

Graham Alexander set for Preston North End January overhaul with loan deals poised to be cancelled

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that preston North End have had a disastrous season so far which has left them rock bottom of the Championship after 15 games.
  • Industry observers note that that leaves them in need of major changes in January, and Alexander is looking to make his mark on the squad.
  • In a recent development, north End currently have four loanees in their squad; Caleb Wiley, Liam Gibbs, Delano Burgzorg and Jusef Erabi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that preston North End have had a disastrous season so far which has left them rock bottom of the Championship after 15 games. PNE are already seven points adrift of safety, with a managerial change to Graham Alexander so far not working out.

Industry observers note that that leaves them in need of major changes in January, and Alexander is looking to make his mark on the squad. According to Pete O’Rourke, the Preston boss is hoping to terminate all his sides loan deals to replace them with his own targets in the winter.

In a recent development, north End currently have four loanees in their squad; Caleb Wiley, Liam Gibbs, Delano Burgzorg and Jusef Erabi. PNE have already brought in Greg Docherty under Alexander but he is clearly far from done with his Preston squad overhaul.

It has been revealed that so far this season all of the PNE loanees have underperformed, which is evident in the Championship table. Erabi has managed just two goals in 15 appearances, while Burgzorg is yet to score despite contributing a handful of assists.

Industry observers note that wiley has shown promise, scoring on his Deepdale debut against Bristol City, but injury has restricted him to five appearances. Gibbs has also struggled for availability, making five appearances before suffering a quad injury that is expected to sideline him for several months.

Industry observers note that returning the four players in January would free up squad places and potentially allow Alexander to recruit players better suited to his preferred system. With the relegation battle intensifying, the manager needs greater reliability and quality from his available options.

Preston North End need to revamp their squad in January. They need something special to turn their season around after what has been a horrendous opening third of the campaign and returning those loanees is a simple way to switch things up.

However, with that said, PNE still need those loanees for another 10 games at least. With the busy festive period coming up, for those players to know that they are not wanted by Alexander might not be ideal.

He needs those players to give them all over the next months or so. Sometimes that can be a wake-up call for some players, who will see this as a time to prove themselves but it can also go in the other way.

PNE have a massive few weeks ahead which include the current loanees, which starts at West Ham this weekend. If Preston cant pickup some points in over December, they are going to be in major trouble no matter what happens in January.

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 00:19.

Nico Paz is reportedly set to spark a tussle for his signature after Mauricio Pochettino's recent appointment at Manchester United.

The 22-year-old Como midfielder stole the show in Argentina's recent emphatic 7-0 friendly rout of Costa Rica during the international break.

Paz opened the scoring with a thunderous long-range strike into the top corner before leaving two defenders in his wake and firing home a powerful effort with his weaker foot to make it 3-0.

Fellow compatriots Julian Alvarez and 19-year-old Fiorentina loanee Franco Mastantuono also struck doubles during the dominant international display.

United supporters are already painfully familiar with the playmaker's long-range prowess after a carbon-copy strike sparked Como's 4-1 Champions League demolition of the Red Devils last month.

According to The Sun, Pochettino's recent arrival in the Old Trafford dugout could hand Manchester United a decisive advantage in their pursuit of his fellow Argentine.

Paz has established himself as one of European football's most coveted young prospects this term, contributing six goals and eight assists to register a direct goal involvement every 81 minutes.

Standing at 6ft 1in, the attacking midfielder combines refined technical quality with the physical resilience required to withstand the relentless intensity of the Premier League.

However, the source above states that prying the former Real Madrid Castilla graduate away from Serie A will prove complicated given that Los Blancos retain an €80m (£66.8m) option to re-sign him in 2027.

United also reportedly face fierce competition from across the continent, with Premier League rivals Arsenal and Chelsea alongside Paris Saint-Germain all closely monitoring his rapid progression.

The source above believes that Pochettino should receive substantial financial backing from the club hierarchy when the winter transfer window opens in January.

While adding a dynamic playmaker of Paz's calibre remains an enticing long-term objective, the Red Devils are initially expected to prioritise recruiting a fresh striker and a defender.

The need for defensive reinforcements has grown increasingly urgent amid reports that Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez wants out of Old Trafford despite earning plaudits for his recent international displays.
