💡 Key Takeaways
  • Below, you can review the leading headlines from and about Germany from Friday, October 30:.
  • Chancellor Friedrich Merz visits the demilitarized zone between North and South Korea.
  • Merz draws on Germany's own reunification experience, saying division causes suffering.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These updates have been closed.

Below, you can review the leading headlines from and about Germany from Friday, October 30:.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz visits the demilitarized zone between North and South Korea.

Merz draws on Germany's own reunification experience, saying division causes suffering.

Two German leaders, two parallel missions across Asia.

While President Frank-Walter Steinmeier sought to reinforce ties with China in Beijing, Chancellor Friedrich Merz toured Japan, South Korea and Singapore, promoting closer cooperation among what he calls the world's "middle powers.".

Together, the visits highlight Berlin's effort to lower risks without decoupling from China.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Germany's annual inflation rate eased to 2.8% in October from 3.3% in September, with economists pointing to the government's fuel tax cut as the main reason.

Industry observers note that preliminary figures from the Federal Statistical Office showed energy prices rose 12.2% compared with a year earlier, down from 14.9% in September. Services inflation slowed to 2.5%, while food inflation remained at 0.4%.

Industry observers note that "The decisive factor was the fuel tax cut," said Silke Tober of the Macroeconomic Policy Institute. The reduction took effect in October and runs through December, although rising crude oil prices partly offset the savings at the pump.

According to recent reports, ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski stated higher energy costs had yet to feed through into broader price increases. Unlike during the 2022 energy crisis, consumers were unwilling or unable to absorb substantially higher prices, he said.

But economists warned the relief could prove temporary. "Gas and oil prices have risen significantly again in recent weeks," noted Stephanie Schoenwald, an economist at Germany's state-owned development bank KfW, citing continuing conflicts and lower inventories.

Recent findings suggest that german President's Frank-Walter Steinmeier latest trip to Asia was intended to provide more clarity. Amid a delicate period, Steinmeier sought a balancing act in China between respect and criticism.

It was a state visit of a kind rarely seen today. For four days, Steinmeier traveled across the country: from Hefei, where the German automaker Volkswagen's China operations are headquartered, through historic villages and the imposing landscapes of the Yellow Mountains. He also visited several points of interest of Chinese history, art, and science, and finally, he headed to Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing's political center.

In a recent development, steinmeier—who is set to leave office in March 2027— spoke as a statesman and diplomat on matters of German and European interest. Chinese President Xi Jinping and Steinmeier have known each other for many years, so in this respect, the president was the right man to address even the most difficult complications as a European.

This political balancing act between respect and criticism did not trigger any visible outrage in Beijing.

When he spoke with Chinese leaders about their subsidies for exports to Europe and the related glitch of the trade deficit, Xi replied: "I am ready to work together to open a upcoming chapter in the comprehensive strategic partnership between our two countries and to advance the development of global governance.".

Just how much willingness lies behind the push for a strategic partnership will become clear during further negotiations between the EU and China.

Xi Jinping seems to understand that a persistent trade deficit with Europe could also become a problem for his country, as an economic crisis in Europe could further strain China's economy.

According to recent reports, as "the world's second- and third-largest economies," China and Germany also bear "an important responsibility for the development of relations between China and Europe, as well as for stable growth in the global economy," Xi Jinping said. While that may not sound like a breakthrough yet, it certainly sounds like an understanding.

In contrast to his economic arguments, Steinmeier's political appeals for Beijing to assume more responsibility for the international order fell on deaf ears.

The German president addressed global conflicts and wars on several occasions in Beijing, including Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine. But he received no responses in official statements.

That same evening, the news channel of the Chinese TV network CCTV aired a report that merely covered Steinmeier's visit to a well-known astrophysics institute.

There was no mention of the call for China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, to do more to promote world peace.

According to recent reports, mitat Özdemir is one of more than 870,000 Turkish workers who were recruited to Germany by a government program between 1961 and 1973. He dealt with tough factory work, language barriers and cultural differences.

Six decades later, he and his family still live in Germany. How did the program from back then shape their lives and modern Germany?

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.

North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.

"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he said.

"You can also notice it here at this place, how much a country suffers from division and how strong the desire is for reunification, at least in this part of the Korean Peninsula," he noted, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience while visiting Seoul.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state.".

A glass cabinet containing memorabilia linked to the 1958 Munich Air Disaster, in which eight Manchester United footballers lost their lives, was smashed and plundered in the Munich suburb of Trudering this week.

The display case on Manchesterplatz forms part of a memorial commemorating the tragedy which occurred when the United team made a refueling stop in Munich while on the way back from a European Cup game in Belgrade, Serbia, on February 6, 1958.

Recent findings suggest that the plane struggled to take off again in the wintery conditions at the old Munich-Riem airport to the east of the city center and, on the third attempt, ploughed off the end of the runway and into a house. Of the 44 people on board, 23 were killed, including eight United players, several journalists and two crew members.

The crash site has become a place of pilgrimage for United supporters and, in 2020, the cabinet was installed on the initiative of the Red Docs Munich – a local Bayern Munich fan club – to house the various memorabilia and tributes left by visitors.

Munich police stated the cabinet was broken into on Monday morning between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (07:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. UTC), with the unknown perpetrators making off with a glass sculpture and several medals.

"They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ifty Ahmed, chairman of the Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF), told the BBC, adding: "Whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories.".

The Red Docs Munich arranged for replacement glass to be installed on the same day. The MMMF said Manchester United had offered to pay for the repairs but said the foundation had covered the costs itself.

The joint commemoration of the 1958 disaster and the maintenance of the memorial site has produced extensive and friendly relations between Bayern Munich and Manchester United, who will meet in the Champions League in January.

German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

It has been revealed that profits of German luxury car brand Audi for the third quarter came plunged 87% year-on-year to €95 million ($106 million), the Volkswagen subsidiary reported on Friday. This is a drop from €718 million seen in the same quarter last year.

The drop comes amid weak demand in China, and US tariffs.

"Market and competitive conditions have become significantly more difficult in the third quarter," Audi chief financial officer Jürgen Rittersberger told journalists on a call.

"That all shows that we need to intensify measures and set clear priorities," he added.

Overall in the first nine months of 2026, Audi's profits have dropped 41% to €1.22 billion.

The carmaker trimmed its 2026 profit outlook down to 3 to 5% for the year, down from the previous 5 to 7%.

Audi's sluggish numbers represent more bad news for the 10-brand Volkswagen Group, which on Thursday reported its largest quarterly loss in more than a ‌decade, at nearly €6 billion.

A ban on new Stolpersteine ("stumbling stones") to commemorate victims of the Holocaust in the eastern German town of Heidenau will be upheld after five petitions against the measure were thrown out.

Local councilors from Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) voted together in September to pass the controversial ban on new stones being laid in the town in Saxony, near Dresden.

Petitions against the measure were submitted from across Germany — as well as one from the Netherlands — calling for victims of the Nazi regime to continue to be remembered in Heidenau by way of the small metal plaques embedded in pavements.

"Not everybody has to like the stumbling stones but everyone should have the possibility to lay one in public," one councilor, Michael Schürer, told Germany's Catholic News Agency (KNA), criticizing the rejection of the petitions.

The initiators of the Heidenau ban had argued that, while remembering Holocaust victims remains essential, the placement of Stolpersteine leads to "passersby walking over or even stepping onto the names of the victims." They suggested honoring victims at a local cemetery instead.

The decision of the local Heidenau CDU to join forces with the AfD to pass the motion sparked a nationwide scandal and furthered the debate over the conservatives' commitment to the political "firewall" against the far right.

Ahead of talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier lauded China's role as a global technological and economic power, while emphasizing the responsibility that comes along with it.

"We both bear responsibility for the ⁠international order ​and for the conditions under which states in this world maintain and shape their relations," Steinmeier noted.

President Xi praised what he called an "all-dimensional strategic partnership" between China and Germany, calling for new cooperation based on stability and mutual benefit.

"This new paradigm sends a positive signal to the world: we favor openness over closure, and cooperation over confrontation," Xi stated during opening remarks, emphasizing the start of a "new chapter" in Germany-China ties.

Xi added that he hopes Germany and the European Union will stick by a "rational, pragmatic and friendly" China policy, adding that cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences in China-EU relations.

The EU has a massive trade deficit with China, which reached €360 billion ($400.4 billion) last year and is set to exceed that level this year.

Brussels has accused China of unfair economic practices, saying its state subsidies for its industries are creating an unlevel playing field. Germany with its export based economy, the EU's largest, is hit hard by China's manufacturing surplus flooding global markets.

Industry groups say the surge in imports from China is leading to an increasing number of factory closures in the bloc.

Nonetheless, "differences and problems can always be resolved," the Chinese president remarked.

Recent findings suggest that on October 30, 1961, West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers. Sixty-five years on, many so-called "guest workers" cannot live from their pensions.

Learn more about how "guest workers" are struggling as they reach retirement age in this in depth report by Oliver Pieper.

While German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in South Korea on Friday called for a better rule-based trade order, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier was in the Chinese capital in a bid to smooth out trade disagreements.

In Beijing, Steinmeier called for preserving the "win-win principle" characterizing Sino-German relations, borrowing from the expression "win-win cooperation," one of the most frequently used phrases in Chinese foreign policy statements.

Germany's economic ties with China have gone through a shock in recent years, with Chinese manufacturing growing into sectors once dominated by German firms, and Chinese electric cars taking over market share.

At the start of a meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, Steinmeier cited a recent deal limiting exports of Chinese hybrid cars to the EU in exchange for select tariff cuts on EU exports to China as an example of a "a way to find solutions.".

Steinmeier also brought up Germany's growing trade deficit with China, which grew to nearly €90 billion ($100 billion) last year.

Industry observers note that germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

It has been revealed that steinmeier remarked Germany would work to solve trade problems with China. "We are coming with the intention of maintaining and strengthening the framework for good economic exchange between our two countries," Steinmeier said.

Later in the day, the German president, who occupies a largely ceremonial role without policymaking power, was also recieved by an honor guard alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During his final day of a whirlwind Asia tour this week, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul on Friday that Germany and Europe are ready to cooperate with Asian economies to foster a rules-based economic order.

Merz mentioned the European Union is ready to take the lead in shaping a better deal for countries in Asia feeling the pressure of a destabilized rules-based trade order.

"Competition between the US and China is ramping up. Tariffs, technological decoupling strategies and a tough race for critical raw materials and fresh technologies are fundamentally changing the rules of our global economy," Merz noted.

Sources indicate that "These conflicts and systemic shifts in power patterns concern us all. They particularly concern economically aspiring partners in the Indo-Pacific, as well as in Germany and in Europe.".

During stops in Singapore and Japan this week, Merz pushed for free trade partnerships and greater European cooperation with Asian economies.

In Singapore on Wednesday, Merz called for a free trade agreement between the EU and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), a sweeping multilateral free trade agreement connecting the Asia Pacific and the Americas.

Industry observers note that the UK is the single European signatory, albeit outside of the EU bloc. The US pulled out during the first administration President Donald Trump in 2017, scuttling the original version, the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP).

"We want to offer opportunities beyond bilateral agreements,"he noted in Seoul on Friday.

"We are resolutely joining forces against unilateralism, autocratic power politics and violations of international law," Merz added.

"When supply chains become political pawns, when access to key technologies is obstructed or when efforts to secure raw materials resemble displays of power rather than fair partnerships, this jeopardizes growth, prosperity and ultimately the security of entire regions.".

Merz also tried to allay concerns about EU protectionism under the "Made in Europe" scheme intended to protect carmakers.

"There is a fear that we might be facing ‌a latest wave of European protectionism - that we are closing ‌ourselves off from other nations," ‌Merz said.

Sources indicate that "I take these concerns very seriously. I will carry them back not just to Berlin, ‌but also to Brussels, and I will certainly raise the fact that these concerns were expressed to me quite forcefully here," he added.

Citing Germany as an example, South Korean Prime Minister Han Seong Sook told the conference  "German companies are using Korea as a central hub to expand their presence in the Asia-Pacific region.".

Additional reporting by Nina Haase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 06:31.

Manchester United have reportedly stepped up their search for a successor to English gem JJ Gabriel, with the Red Devils making the signing of a Ligue 1 prodigy their priority.

It was an open secret, but it is now official. In a message posted on his Instagram account, JJ Gabriel confirmed his departure from Manchester United.

Unwilling to sign his first professional contract with the Red Devils, because of a lack of recognition that has prevented him from playing a single game for the first team, the 16-year-old hopeful has no shortage of suitors for the next stage of a career that is only just beginning.

Recent findings suggest that wanted by Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and Bayern Munich, JJ Gabriel is at the moment tipped to join Real Madrid in a deal estimated at around £12.8m (€15m). For their part, the Red Devils, now managed by Argentine boss Mauricio Pochettino, have probably anticipated the loss of their attacking midfielder for some time.

He scored 34 goals in 35 games in all competitions with the various youth teams without ever breaking into the first team.

Behind the scenes, the Old Trafford club appear to have already made a decision on a successor for JJ Gabriel.

According to information from ManUtd Addicts, relayed by the specialist website Africa Foot, Manchester United want to sign a Ligue 1 prodigy: Mezian Mesloub. Very advanced talks have reportedly taken place over the Lens player’s arrival in England.

It has been revealed that while no deadline has been mentioned, the Portuguese hopeful could reportedly be signed by Manchester United before being loaned straight back to Lens. The English club would thus get their hands on the player ahead of the other suitors, while allowing Lens to keep him for some time yet.

A product of the Gaillette academy, Mezian Mesloub made his first-team debut in the 2025-26 season, in the 33rd Ligue 1 game against Nantes (1-0), when he made his mark by scoring the only goal of the match shortly after coming on.

But it is above all this season, 2026-27, that his playing time has increased sharply: eight games, including five in Ligue 1, one start and one assist in Lens’ only Champions League win so far, away at Slavia Prague (3-2).

While it is probably inconceivable for Lens to part with Mesloub so rapidly, his progress and contract situation inevitably attract interest.

Industry observers note that wanted by Benfica and PSV Eindhoven, the Martigues native signed his first professional contract last summer, until June 2030, with last season’s Ligue 1 runners-up to Paris Saint-Germain. That gives Lens hope of one day making a very good sale for a player whose market value rose from just £425,000 (€500,000) to £6.8m (€8m) between June and September 2026.

Man United news: Neville backs Dalot and names three defenders to sell before him

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 06:43.
  • Diogo Dalot has become one of the targets of Manchester United supporters’ dissatisfaction, but Gary Neville believes the Portuguese full-back is far from being one of the squad’s main problems.
  • The former Manchester United captain came out in defence of his fellow right-back after the boos Dalot received at Old Trafford and stated he would get rid of other players before parting with the number two.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 06:43.

Diogo Dalot has become one of the targets of Manchester United supporters’ dissatisfaction, but Gary Neville believes the Portuguese full-back is far from being one of the squad’s main problems.

The former Manchester United captain came out in defence of his fellow right-back after the boos Dalot received at Old Trafford and stated he would get rid of other players before parting with the number two.

In a recent development, the criticism comes at a time of instability for Manchester United, who are struggling to find consistency in the Premier League and are again facing questions over the individual performances of their players. Dalot was one of the negative protagonists in the draw with Aston Villa, particularly because of the penalty he conceded, and his substitution during the game was greeted with celebrations by the home fans.

According to recent reports, ‘I would be getting rid of some players before Dalot. Dalot got booed last week at Old Trafford and I was really surprised at that’ - the former full-back remarked on the ‘Stick to Football’ podcast.

In Neville’s view, Dalot is receiving excessive criticism for frequently playing out of his natural position. The Portuguese is a right-back, but has also been used on the left side, either as a full-back or wing-back, depending on the team’s needs.

The former Manchester United player stressed that this change of role requires adaptation and that Dalot demonstrates a positive attitude in accepting the tasks given to him by the manager.

‘If you put me at left wing-back or left-back, and I am a right-back, and he is too, I would say: “No way, why are you putting me there?”’.

The pundit, however, believes Dalot has shown a willingness to help the team, even when he has to play in a position different from the one in which he feels most comfortable.

Sources indicate that ‘Instead, Dalot literally sticks his hand up and says: “Go on, I’ll play there, I will do anything for the team”. I never see him shirk anything, I never look at him and think he could try harder’ - he added.

Sources indicate that neville’s defence does not mean the full-back is free from criticism of his performances. The Portuguese struggled against Aston Villa and conceded a penalty that contributed to the result. The former captain, however, believes individual performance needs to be analysed within the context of a squad with collective problems and players often shifted out of their usual roles.

According to recent reports, neville also compared Dalot with other members of Manchester United’s defensive unit and said there are players who should be sold before the Portuguese. The former full-back specifically named Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt.

‘I watch defenders very closely and, if you ask me, I would be getting rid of Mazraoui, well gone, before him, I would be getting rid of Martinez well before him, I would be getting rid of De Ligt gone before him.’.

The opinion stands out because the three players named have also faced questions at different points of the season. Mazraoui has been used in different defensive roles, while Martinez has dealt with injury problems and controversy. De Ligt, meanwhile, has also been subject to the team’s fluctuations in performance and changes to the defensive set-up.

Dalot joined Manchester United in 2018 from Porto and has had different spells at the club. After a loan at Milan, he returned to Old Trafford and earned a place in the team, particularly during the 2022-23 season. Since then, he has become a regular presence, although his use on both sides of defence has fuelled debate about his best position.

While the club try to find stability, the Portuguese remains a recurring option in defence. For Neville, the pressure on the full-back should not be greater than that directed at other players who, in his assessment, have performed worse or contributed less to the team’s needs.

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5726 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points.
  • When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

In a recent development, it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

It has been revealed that any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

According to recent reports, since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

According to recent reports, cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

According to recent reports, alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

In a recent development, “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Sources indicate that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose noted. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

It has been revealed that speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

Recent findings suggest that his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Sources indicate that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he stated: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He mentioned: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola noted: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most key one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

In a recent development, liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

Industry observers note that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tom Iorpenda was one of the EFL's brightest talents last season while at Notts County, but the 21-year-old has yet to see the pitch in any competition so far this year.

The former Brighton and Huddersfield Town academy product ended a five-year association with the Terriers this past summer, signing for Swansea City for around £1 million towards the end of the transfer window.

Iorpenda had played every game in league and play-off action for Notts in their League Two promotion campaign while on loan from Huddersfield last term, and returned to the Accu Stadium with plenty of momentum and a possible route into first-team action.

In the end, with his contract up at the end of the season, Huddersfield opted to cash in on the versatile midfielder and insert a sell-on clause so they could profit further down the line, instead of possibly losing him for free.

It's safe to say it hasn't worked out yet at all, which must be a real frustration for the League One pair.

It has been revealed that it's always difficult when a young star arrives at a club in the latter stages of the summer transfer window. Iorpenda spent the whole summer and pre-season with Huddersfield, signing for the Swans on August 30.

Swansea adopted a much more intense play style ahead of Vitor Matos' second season in charge in South Wales. They rank first in pressing sequences, high turnovers and have the lowest PPDA (passes per defensive action) in the Championship.

That's difficult to get up to speed with when you have a full pre-season, let alone when you don't.

Additionally, Iorpenda joined a Swansea side that, at the time, had won two and drawn one of their first three games and were about to make it three wins from four against Watford on September 1.

So, the 21-year-old arrived at the club with just two Championship appearances under his belt, totalling 50 minutes, from his time at Huddersfield, has had to get up to speed with their intensity and has been trying to dislodge what has been a winning lineup.

It's been difficult, and that's the reason why he still has no appearances so far in a Swansea shirt.

According to recent reports, iorpenda was everywhere for Notts last year. He predominantly played as an attacking midfielder, but Martin Paterson trusted him to man the engine room a bit further back, too, and as loan spells go, it was one of the best in the EFL last year.

Not only did Iorpenda start 46 of the 49 league and play-off games at Meadow Lane last season, but he also scored three and assisted eight, including setting up Jayden Luker (another loanee set for bigger things) for the only goal over two legs in the play-off semi-final against Chesterfield.

It has been revealed that per FotMob, he ranked in the top 3% of players in his position for defensive contributions, duels won and tackles, but also in the top 5% for touches, passes and fouls won. He operated mainly in the left channel, but he covered ground better than most could in League Two that year.

Notts County would have likely had Iorpenda right at the top of their summer wishlist after they secured promotion from League Two last season, no matter how unrealistic the signing appeared to be. He was ready to propel himself up the leagues, and perhaps the Magpies could have been entrusted to continue his development in the tier above.

It has been revealed that how disappointing has it been to see Tom Iorpenda hardly play this season, Notts fans? Let us know in the comments.

Unfortunately, the 21-year-old's contract situation worked against them, and now they're being forced to see him ride the bench in the Championship.

Iorpenda's stock has fallen quite significantly since he joined Swansea, which doesn't bode well for a Huddersfield side who felt they could have been earning a little more than the £1m they pocketed in the original sale.

It's unknown what contract talks were held between the midfielder and Huddersfield over the summer, but from his lack of inclusion in any side under Martin Drury to start the season, it was clear he wasn't favoured.

Even the Terriers couldn't deny that he has potential, though, and a £1m + sell-on clause actually went down as a good deal for both sides. Swansea got a high-potential player for cheap, and Huddersfield banked a seven-figure fee for a guy they could have lost for nothing at the end of the season.

At the moment, though, they aren't getting any more than that base amount, as Iorpenda is yet to showcase any Championship quality just yet, mainly because he's had no chance to showcase anything.

Notts will be looking on, annoyed that their ex-loan star isn't enjoying life elsewhere, while the dreams of making some more money immediately from Huddersfield's side aren't coming to fruition, either.

In a recent development, however, it's not as if Iorpenda has been left out of squads altogether. He's making the bench, just not getting on the pitch. In the 12 games he's been available for, he's made the 20-man squad in half of those.

He'll be one of the players looking to impress whoever the newhead coach turns out to be, after Vitor Matos left Swansea on Wednesday to take charge at Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg.

A potential new playstyle could be implemented that benefits Iorpenda, or the new boss could simply come into the job with a fresh slate, and the ex-Huddersfield man won't already be battling with settled starters.

Either way, it may only be a matter of time before Iorpenda gets to see the pitch in a Swansea shirt for the first time, and those at Huddersfield and Notts County who have cringed at his involvement so far will hope he can make a name for himself when he does.

Sebastien Pocognoli has backed Ben Gannon-Doak to find his killer instinct in the final third and establish himself as Scotland’s main man.

The Bournemouth youngster had an up-and-down evening in Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win over North Macedonia, getting into numerous promising positions on the right flank and winning the penalty – dispatched by John McGinn – which decided the game.

But, as has been the case throughout his Scotland career, the 21-year-old’s final ball in key moments left a lot to be desired.

Pocognoli is under no illusions that Gannon-Doak still has plenty to improve on, but insists that it won’t be long before things start to click for the talented youngster.

Recent findings suggest that ‘As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one v ones I am happy,’ stated the Belgian. ‘With Ben, we know that he is at a young age and needs to work on specific things.

In a recent development, ‘On Friday, he had great opportunities. We know that he needs to improve on the end product, but he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets Ben Gannon-Doak as he is substituted at Hampden.

‘He did that last night as well. We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball. I am happy with his performance.

Sources indicate that ‘He is a young lad, just 21. Okay, he has become more mature than he was, but I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making.

It has been revealed that ‘I believe if he is playing every game he can make many decisions. He will know that in the next game he will have to do it again.

‘If he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks, sometimes he can think, “This is my moment”.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It is a process. He will become older and at some point will become relaxed in his decision making, but at this very young age what he is producing is very good.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I say exactly the same thing to him after training on the pitch. I say, “Ben, this is the next step”. He knows that and it is important he knows that.’.

Scotland conclude their Nations League campaign in Switzerland on Monday knowing that only a victory against the group winners will be enough if they are to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia – presently one point better off ahead of their trip to North Macedonia – into second spot.

Pocognoli admits Gannon-Doak's end product has to improve after another frustrating show.

Should that happen, Scotland would have a crack at earning promotion to League A via a play-off in March, and also crucially guarantee their place as a Pot 2 side for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

‘We are still alive in this competition,’ said Pocognoli, who celebrated his first win at Hampden on Friday at the third time of asking. ‘We know we have to do more than this competition. This competition is about trying to build something.

‘But it is nice to have that possibility on Monday to try to create something against one of the top 20 teams in the world.

‘We need to try to be brave. Switzerland have already qualified so let’s go there and be smart because they are a good team.

Industry observers note that ‘It is part of the process to play away against a top team. That is not something we have done yet. The approach will be different and, for me as a coach, it is a game with a lot of responsibility.’.

Latest Update: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • According to recent reports, "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • In a recent development, the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

According to recent reports, "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

In a recent development, the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Industry observers note that names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

Industry observers note that "A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

In a recent development, but a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, shows how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

Names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer stated their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

Research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

"Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

Even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

Sources indicate that pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

Industry observers note that "People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

Later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she said.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

In a recent development, tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

It has been revealed that but the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

It has been revealed that "I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

But Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum stated.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

That does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Recent findings suggest that online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

It has been revealed that pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

Now the next task is to replicate that on the road, where they've failed to win since their first away game of the season against West Ham United, but it won't be easy against a Wolves side who are within touching distance of top spot.

There are still parts of the Old Gold fanbase who are sceptical of head coach Cesar Peixoto, but one thing they can agree on is that, Bolton Wanderers aside, they've been well in control of their home games this season.

Both sides will be keen to take all three points, but these eight players won't be available to help do so.

The key injury in the Wolves camp remains with Raul Jimenez, with the veteran striker set to miss the rest of the calendar year after going in for knee surgery in mid-October.

The 35-year-old rejoined the club this past summer after three years at Fulham, where he still showcased his Premier League goalscoring qualities, netting 28 league goals in those three seasons.

He scored three in his first six back at Molineux, but isn't close to being able to add to that.

In a recent development, left-back Ghislain Konan was brought to Wolves in the summer from Gil Vicente, reuniting with Cesar Peixoto in the first place. The 30-year-old provided some much-needed experience, with 59 Ivorian caps throughout his career.

However, Konan hasn't gotten going in the Old Gold just yet, and after just three appearances, he was sidelined until late December after picking up an MCL injury.

Charlton boss Nathan Jones was as coy as ever when discussing injuries ahead of the trip to Wolves, stating that those who missed Sheffield United are "closer than they were two weeks ago," and instead putting the focus on those who came in to replace those injured players.

Club captain Lloyd Jones was absent from a league squad for the first time this season against the Blades. He'd played every minute up until then. The hip injury he picked up could see him back this weekend, but he remains a doubt.

Karlarn Grant has also been a key part of Nathan Jones' side since making his return to the side he came through the academy with this past summer.

He was also absent from a league squad for the first time this season with a back matter last time out.

Nathaniel Chalobah was the third absentee from that win over Sheffield United after picking up a thigh injury.

It's the latest setback in what has been a troubling few years for the 31-year-old. He's already missed two months of the current season with a similar issue, and only played just over 1,000 minutes of league action across two years at Sheffield Wednesday prior to his summer move to the Valley, due to injury, too.

Sources indicate that reece Burke is another in the Charlton squad who has battled injury problems throughout his career. He reunited with ex-Luton Town boss Jones ahead of last season, having played fewer than 27 league games per year in his four campaigns with the Hatters.

He only managed 17 appearances last season and has yet to see the pitch this year after suffering an innocuous injury ahead of an EFL Cup match with Tottenham Hotspur back in August.

Charlton are more transparent with their long-term setbacks. Rob Apter is one of those, with a knee injury picked up a month ago, sidelining him for "an extended spell.".

Kenyan centre-back Collins Sichenje will miss the remainder of the campaign after he suffered an ACL injury during that aforementioned EFL Cup tie at Tottenham back in August.

The 23-year-old has only made 10 appearances since his mid-season move from Vojvodina last term.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mansfield Town have made a decision to decrease the capacity of the One Call Stadium, otherwise known as Field Mill, after a meeting with the Safety Advisory Group.

The Stags are currently in the midst of a third successive campaign in League One, with Nigel Clough's side amassing 19 points from 12 matches.

As a result of the club's recent trajectory, Mansfield have welcomed several fallen giants to this part of Nottinghamshire.

Stags fans have developed a reputation for generating plenty of noise, which, in turn, has led to a strong atmosphere with those backing the visiting sides housed in the stadium's North Stand.

However, the decision, which has been made ahead of Saturday's clash with MK Dons, hasn't gone down well with several fans.

The One Call Stadium is currently the fifth-smallest stadium in League One, with only the home grounds of Cambridge United, Stevenage, Burton Albion and Bromley able to house fewer spectators.

Attendances so far this season have been at the 8,527 mark on average, but Mansfield will now see fewer visiting supporters pass through the turnstiles.

A statement from Nottinghamshire Council on Friday confirmed that the stadium's North Stand will be reduced in capacity from 1,000 to 600 following incidents relating to crowd management and control in the EFL Trophy clash against Chesterfield, which the League Two side won 5-3.

Mansfield have since confirmed the agreement in conjunction with the council and Safety Advisory Group, but also confirmed that the club are exploring the possibility of a safe-standing area within the stand.

Although this decision doesn't have a major impact on the matchday experience of the home support at the One Call Stadium, other than the fact there are fewer visiting fans to engage in back-and-forth with, it has caused plenty of responses.

One Stags supporter wrote: "SAG vs Mansfield Town yet again. Do they ever work with the club rather than against it?".

Recent findings suggest that "But why? What was remarked in the meeting? Away fans getting punished by the SAG which reflects on the club? They deserve a bit of clarity," another commented.

"Poor decision and tbh, it’s rarely full," backed up the feeling of confusion as to why such measures have been taken.

Another Mansfield fan debated: "Surely (has) to be done up and down the country then?

Recent findings suggest that "There is literally nothing wrong with away fans standing up. SAG need to give their head a wobble," was one of many strong reactions.

With Mansfield's last two home games coming against the Spireites and Notts County, another questioned: "Did SAG not look at who the last 3 games have been against at home? At least 2 they should’ve known it would’ve been an matter.".

It has been revealed that one of the potential fans visiting from Buckinghamshire on Saturday stated: "What('s) wrong with standing up? No need to close off part of the stand because of it.".

Sources indicate that what do you make of Mansfield Town's decision to reduce the One Call Stadium's capacity? Comment below!

Industry observers note that however, a Port Vale fan agreed with the decision, replying: "The ticket regulations say that fans should be sitting down. If they stand up and refuse to sit then have them thrown out. If they refuse to leave then have police arrest them. Don't punish other fans because there are some idiots.".

Although Mansfield clarified that the allocation will be temporarily reduced, it has already been debated for how long this will be the case.

Recent fixtures have clearly impacted this decision, and some of League One's largest fanbases could be left scrambling for tickets depending on how long such measures are in place.

Indeed, the Stags are still yet to host the likes of Barnsley, Sheffield Wednesday and Leicester City, with it not exactly being an arduous journey for those who follow the Tykes, Owls and Foxes to make.

Ironically, the decision to house fewer away supporters could still play to the advantage of Clough's side, who have picked up the majority of their points so far on home turf.

By Lewis Blain | 19 Nov 2026 07:21.

Manchester United are preparing to strengthen their attack in the January transfer window, with upcoming boss Mauricio Pochettino already keen to add more firepower.

The Argentine is understood to have put four main centre-forward targets on his winter 'wishlist', including a prolific striker also attracting interest from former club and top-flight rivals Tottenham Hotspur.

Benfica talisman Vangelis Pavlidis has emerged as a particularly exciting possibility after an outstanding start to the season in Portugal.

The Red Devils are ready to spend significantly to back Pochettino in January, with Benfica striker Pavlidis among the names under consideration, according to reports.

Spurs and Barcelona have also been linked with the Greece international, who is remarked to be open to a move to the Premier League in 2027.

One source revealed: "Pochettino is eager to make sure United have more of a goal threat. He's already been discussing names, and Vangelis Pavlidis is someone who fits the bill.".

Pavlidis is not the only striker on United's radar, with Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen also admired by Pochettino. However, a deal for the Nigerian is considered less realistic due to his substantial transfer fee and wage demands.

Former Brentford forward Ivan Toney is another option, while Borussia Dortmund's Serhou Guirassy is being monitored as a potential rotation option, too.

Pavlidis has scored 19 goals in 19 appearances across all competitions this season, while also providing four assists. His remarkable return means he has found the net once every 72 minutes on average.

The 27-year-old's immense goalscoring numbers make him an attractive proposition for United, particularly with Benjamin Sesko having struggled with injuries.

His current form suggests he could provide an immediate improvement to Pochettino's attacking options, offering a reliable source of goals during the second half of the campaign.

Importantly, Pavlidis' age does not necessarily have to come at the expense of Sesko's long-term development, with the Slovenian still viewed as part of United's future once fully fit.

Osimhen may be the more ambitious acquisition, but Pavlidis appears to offer a potentially more attainable solution without sacrificing significant attacking quality.

If United are serious about challenging at the top end of the Premier League, adding a striker with 19 goals already this season could be a major step forward.

Barnsley have confirmed that adult tickets for their game against Huddersfield Town next month will cost £35.

The Tykes have had a tough season so far, with Daniel Stendel’s return to Oakwell not producing the results that many had hoped, as the team sit in the relegation zone.

However, many fans recognise that Barnsley’s problems run deeper right now, and there are calls for the owners to leave the club.

And, that has ignited again, with the club confirming that adult tickets for the home clash against Huddersfield on December 19 will be £35.

This was always going to be a game that was priced higher than most, as there is a rivalry between the two Yorkshire clubs - and it’s worth noting it’s the same pricing structure as the one they went with against Sheffield Wednesday.

Plus, with Huddersfield flying high, they are likely to shift a lot of tickets, so Barnsley, who will be charging the visitors £35 as well, will see this as a chance to make money.

Firstly, it should be mentioned that problems with ticket prices are not exclusive to Barnsley, and fans of clubs up and down the country would want their own clubs to review prices.

But, in this instance, you can understand why Barnsley fans are furious, as £35 is an awful lot of money to watch a League One fixture.

Yes, it’s a game against a local side, but Barnsley are battling to stay in the third tier right now, so they should be doing all they can to bring supporters back, which isn’t going to happen when you’re charging £35.

It has been revealed that plus, this is a game that will be played a week before Christmas, at a time when money is tight for everyone. When you combine that with the fixture being televised, it really is a poor decision from Barnsley, who are prioritising money over fans.

Again, they’re by no means the only club to do that, but it’s a shame that they aren’t going the other way and trying to do affordable deals to entice supporters back.

Of course, the hierarchy will argue that they need to bring in funds to help the club, but it’s always about striking the right balance and making fans feel valued.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:03 EST, 14 November 2026.

Amid the clamour for a change at the helm following another poor showing at a major tournament, it was easy to lose sight of the reality of the situation.

According to recent reports, steve Clarke didn’t crash and burn in the US because a raft of world-class talents failed to turn up on the biggest stage. It happened primarily because a limited squad was unable to outperform two top-ten nations in Brazil and Morocco who could call upon infinitely superior footballers.

Sebastian Pocognoli has since arrived on the scene having earned a stellar reputation from his title success with Union Saint-Gilloise and his less feted spell at Monaco. But he has not come armed with a magic wand.

In opening the door to a string of fresh faces and advocating the more attacking approach which so many craved, the turbulence he’s experienced to date should only have been expected.

Limited by both the standard of players who are eligible for Scotland and the time he has to work with them, only the blissfully naïve would have seen his appointment as a quick fix.

While there were some positives to be taken from the game with North Macedonia – primarily the result – it’s likely the nation will have to endure more short-term pain for long-term gain.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets his players after a satisfactory evening at Hampden.

This was always going to take time, perhaps, in the view of John McGinn, more than many may have imagined.

‘The manager’s got a great reputation, a good record at both places he’s been,’ said the Aston Villa captain. ‘The most important thing now in football is individuals don’t win you games. It’s unity, teamwork and everyone being on the same page.

‘You see how successful clubs and successful countries do it. And we want to be one of them.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s not going to happen overnight. There’s a lot to learn but we did create major chances against North Macedonia where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story.

According to recent reports, ‘But this isn’t something that gets fixed in March or even next September. It will start to build over the next 18 months.’.

According to recent reports, if that predicted time frame might raise an eyebrow or two, McGinn makes no apology for it. Call it managing expectations from the midfielder if you please. But without a degree of patience from the Tartan Army, he feels Pocognoli’s ideas won’t take root.

Industry observers note that ‘I understand it’s frustrating,’ he added. ‘It’s freezing and you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there.

McGinn sends his penalty home to give Scotland a deserved lead against North Macedonia.

‘They’re entitled to their opinion, but there’s got to be a mixture of patience.

It has been revealed that ‘The supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys and just let the young ones flourish and try and settle into the team.’.

Give credit where it’s due. With Clarke accused of causing stagnation by selecting the same old faces, Pocognoli has capped five players for the first time while recalling the likes of Oli McBurnie.

Industry observers note that the sages in the stands can’t have it both ways. If the squad was going to evolve, it was never going to be a smooth ride.

According to recent reports, ‘I think the young players are starting to show more now,’ McGinn stressed. ‘Luke Graham on Friday night, I thought he was brilliant. It’s not easy playing in the middle of a back three. He’s been waiting for his chance and the manager’s shown that if you deserve your chance you’re going to get put in there.

In a recent development, ‘We’ve got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to the pitch.’.

It has been revealed that even in victory, McGinn doesn’t dispute that there is significant scope for improvement. He’s convinced, however, that this will all come good in the end.

McGinn insists it's vital the entire Scotland squad buy into the methods of manager Pocognoli.

‘We need to play slightly better,’ he said. ‘We know that, but we’re going through a period which I’ve been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to.

Industry observers note that ‘And it’s about sticking at it. We’re keen to play a style of football that’s not easy but is going to get bums off seats. It’s crucial that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn’t believe in it, that’s when it all starts to fall apart.’.

Industry observers note that friday was another memorable night on a personal level for McGinn. Having broken the tension with the opener only to see North Macedonia level, he held his nerve to put Scotland back from the penalty spot.

The brace put him on 24 international goals, now within six of Denis Law and Kenny Dalglish. But all of that is for another day.

Industry observers note that ‘It feels a bit strange, but at the minute that’s gone to the back burner,’ he stressed. ‘I had a wee chat with Scott (McTominay) about the penalties. I was designated penalty taker but, to be fair, he’s not missed one I don’t think in his career.

‘So, we had a wee chat and I think we both said the most notable thing was just no matter who hit it, hit the back of the net.’.

McGinn is eyeing three points against Switzerland in St Gallen to close the campaign on a high.

It has been revealed that tomorrow, the equation is clear. To finish second in the Nations League group and secure a place in pot two for the Euro draw, Scotland must beat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t beat North Macedonia.

Even if everything clicks for Pocognoli’s side, it will be the tallest of orders.

‘Difficult,’ remarked McGinn. ‘I know they drew on Friday night (with Slovenia) but they’ve got a couple of players back that they were missing last time.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It is a tough one but we want to be competing against these teams away from home. It’s not going to be perfect for a while, but we’ll stick at it.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old on Sunday when he finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

The previous recordholder was Germany's Sebastian Vettel, who first became a world champion at age 23 in 2010.

Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953.

It has been revealed that "I'm speechless. I’m trying to process what has just happened," noted Antonelli after finishing the race.

His parents and sister were there to embrace him when he stepped out of the car.

He was then mobbed by his pit crew.

Industry observers note that "It's been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max ​and Lewis is truly incredible. And looking forward to some more battles in the future," the 20-year-old noted.

Antonelli, who secured the title with four races remaining, said the final lap was complicated by the excitement of what he had achieved.

Recent findings suggest that "I think I lost two seconds because I could not see ahead, I think I saw two Ferraris," he mentioned. "It was very special, a lot of memories went through my mind at that moment, and I let it all out after achieving one of my biggest dreams.".

Antonelli has now risen to 380 points with four races remaining. Verstappen (261) snuck past Hamilton (259) in the standings, but they will be racing for second the rest of the ​way.

Antonelli started the race in ​fourth and needed to finish ‌ninth or better to secure the championship on Sunday no matter what his peers did.

He had a relatively smooth run, though the race was interrupted by a red flag around Lap ​45 when Valtteri Bottas crashed.

Verstappen, meanwhile, claimed his sixth victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix, further cementing his affinity with the circuit.

After Mexico, F1 will head to Brazil and then to Las Vegas.

It has been revealed that the final two Grands Prix are scheduled to be held in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. But it remains uncertain whether they will take place, given the geopolitical instability in the region.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former West Ham United midfielder Reece Oxford has returned to English football, as he signed a deal with League One side, Bromley.

The midfielder first caught the eye with the Hammers in the early stages of his professional career, as he produced an eye-catching display in his senior debut against Arsenal in August 2015.

Oxford became West Ham's youngest-ever Premier League player at 16 years and 236 days old, and his performance looked as though he'd been playing regularly in the top-flight.

West Ham ran out 2-0 winners at the Emirates against Arsenal in that match, and Oxford came in for high praise from Sky Sports' co-commentator on the day, Niall Quinn.

“He’s been phenomenal. A star is born,” Sky Sports co-commentator Niall Quinn said. “He’s been mature, he’s ordering people around. It’s unbelievable to see. He’s mobile, he gets around and he knows the game. He’s a natural.”.

Oxford went on to label his performance as a 'dream debut' in the win over the Gunners, and an 'honour' to play for West Ham in the top-flight.

Sources indicate that “It was a dream debut,” Oxford told Sky Sports. “It’s an honour to play for West Ham and to be the youngest.”.

Oxford is now 27-years-old, and it's fair to say that his career hasn't quite hit the heights that he and supporters would have originally hoped to see.

Whilst contracted to West Ham, he had loan spells with Reading whilst they were in the Championship, before two brief spells with German side Borussia Mönchengladbach, before having his final loan spell with FC Augsburg.

Sources indicate that he seemingly made a good impression with Augsburg as well, as he went on to sign for them on a permanent basis in 2019. Oxford then spent six years in Germany with them, making 80 appearances in total across all competitions.

The former England youth international's time with Augsburg came to an end at the end of the 2024/25 season, when he departed when his contracted expired.

According to recent reports, can you see Reece Oxford's move to Bromley kickstarting his career again? Let us know in the comments!

The midfielder had a year out of competitive football, and it'll be interesting to see if he can recapture his best form, as he's a player with real quality when at his best, which we saw with both West Ham and Augsburg.

There will be some doubts whether he can do that though, as Oxford hasn't played a competitive match since November 2022, as he's had numerous injury problems which have stalled his development in senior football.

A move to Bromley could be the ideal move for him, although the League One side are struggling in their efforts to avoid relegation back into League Two.

Bromley are next in action on Saturday, when they travel to the Select Car Leasing Stadium to take on Reading, in what will be Oxford's first trip back to his former club.

Bromley have found it tough to build any sort of momentum this season, as they're bottom of the League One table, as well as being three points adrift of safety heading into this weekend's fixtures.

This dismal run of form includes being winless from their last 11 matches, and it's a tough ask for them to end that run against a Reading side that have only lost once at home so far in the 2026/27 season.

Oxford has a point to prove at this level, having not played this far down the English football pyramid, but if he can hit the ground running, then Bromley will have a great player on their hands.
